milestone.title: mp-runner skill — executing + fixing, claim/execute sub-mode and fix/remediate sub-mode

intent.outcome: After this ships, the `mp-runner` skill is the role-specific deep-dive for the runner agent (the executing + fixing role per the two-agent / four-role architecture and the 12-stage mp-flow timeline). The skill covers the runner's domain in mp-flow: stages 5-7 (Claim & execute → Self-review → Complete) and stage 9 (Remediate). Two sub-modes: executing (stages 5-7, including round-1 self-review at stage 6 per the L5 lesson and the user's 2026-07-07 clarification that the runner does round-1 self-review) and fixing (stage 9, after coordinator's round-2 review at stage 8). Plus the evidence hygiene discipline (per-run audit record, never overwritten without --force), the commit hygiene, the atomic-write best practices (M113 lessons), and the hand-off contract to the coordinator (M123 four hand-off points).

problem.description: The two-agent / four-role architecture has a runner role but no canonical skill for it. The existing `master-planner` skill is for planning (a coordinator sub-mode); there's no skill that walks the runner through claim → implement → mark step done → pass AC → complete → hand off, and the fix cycle (read findings → patch → resolve) is also unaddressed. The M113 atomic-write lessons (advisory flock lock around plan writes) and the M117 verifier cancellation (killpg on per-AC timeout) need a role-home. M98's monolithic mp-flow had the executing-specific stages mixed with the cross-role timeline; the deep-dive of executing+fixing belongs in its own skill.

in_scope: `templates/skills/mp-runner/SKILL.md` (the role identity) — when an agent session is in runner role, the harness loads `mp-flow` + `mp-runner`. The SKILL.md is the role's identity, the sub-mode map, the stage ownership table (the runner owns mp-flow stages 5 Claim & execute, 6 Self-review, 7 Complete, 9 Remediate), the hand-off contract to the coordinator (with cross-link to M123), and the evidence hygiene discipline.

`templates/skills/mp-runner/executing.md` (executing sub-mode) — the deep-dive of mp-flow stages 5-7 (Claim & execute → Self-review → Complete). The five concrete mp commands: (1) claim = `mp milestone set-status <id> in-progress`; (2) step done = `mp milestone step done <id> <step-id>` for each step; (3) criterion pass = `mp milestone ac criterion pass <id> <ac-id> --evidence "..."`; (4) self-review = `mp reviews finding add <id> --phase self --description "..."` for self-flagged issues, with the lesson-pattern pre-screen checklist from `docs/code-review-lessons.md` (the M99 mp-code-review skill ships the procedural wrapper; the patterns themselves are a deferred work item); (5) complete = `mp milestone complete <id> --evidence "..."` (transitions to `self-reviewed` lifecycle state). The evidence hygiene rule: the `evidence` field is the per-run audit record, never overwritten without --force (per M107 design choice).

`templates/skills/mp-runner/fixing.md` (fixing sub-mode) — the deep-dive of mp-flow stage 9 (Remediate). Reading the coordinator's findings: `mp reviews finding list <id>`. Patching the code. Marking findings resolved: `mp reviews finding resolve <id> <finding-id>`. Re-verifying: `mp milestone verify`. The session-boundary rule: the runner session that produced the code (stages 5-7) is NOT the same session that fixes the coordinator's findings (stage 9) — per L5. The session-boundary protocol is cross-linked from M123 (the hand-off protocol between stages 8 and 9).

`templates/skills/mp-runner/atomic-writes.md` (atomic-write discipline) — references the M113 advisory flock lock + the M117 killpg-on-timeout contract. The runner's run-mode code is `mp milestone complete` and `mp milestone step done`; both go through the lock. The skill documents the contract (no parallel mp invocations on the same milestone) and the killpg contract (per-AC timeout is a SIGKILL to the process group, not a single-pid kill). Note: atomic-writes.md is a cross-cutting contract (applies to BOTH executing and fixing sub-modes), not a sub-mode per se.

Sub-skill integration test: a session loads `mp-flow` + `mp-runner` and walks a fixture milestone through stages 5 → 6 → 7 → 9. Verifies the cross-mode hand-off is functional, not just documented. The fix cycle (stage 9) uses a fresh runner session per the L5 session-boundary rule — verified by a distinct test process or session id.
`mp install --skills=mp-runner` deploys the role identity + sub-mode references. No sub-skill bundle needed (the runner has no existing sub-skills; the deep-dive content ships in M122 itself).
out_of_scope: External reviewing (stages 8 + 10) — coordinator's role, lives in M121's reviewing sub-mode. The runner's reviewing activity is limited to round-1 self-review (stage 6) within executing.md; the deeper external review (stage 8) and re-review (stage 10) are coordinator-only. Per the user's 2026-07-07 clarification: the runner does round-1 self-review at stage 6; the coordinator does round-2 external review at stage 8.
The M113 advisory flock lock + the M117 killpg contract as code changes — both are already shipped; M122 just documents them in atomic-writes.md.
Cross-role orchestration timeline — M120 (mp-flow). M122 references the 12-stage timeline; M122 doesn't redefine the stages.
The hand-off protocol deep-dive (what data passes, what session-boundary, what evidence at the four hand-off points) — M123.

The Pattern: blocks for L6/L8/L13/L14/L15 (the runnable lesson-pattern library from M99) — deferred. The narrative lessons in `docs/code-review-lessons.md` are the runnable surface until the pattern blocks ship; the runner's self-review checklist references the narrative lessons.

design_decisions.area: Two sub-modes (executing, fixing) instead of one (the runner's role):
design_decisions.choice: Two sub-mode files (executing.md, fixing.md) under `templates/skills/mp-runner/`. SKILL.md is the role identity and stage ownership table: the runner owns mp-flow stages 5-7 (executing sub-mode) and stage 9 (fixing sub-mode). The harness loads the role identity; the agent opens the sub-mode file when entering that stage. Round-1 self-review (stage 6) is part of the executing sub-mode per the user's 2026-07-07 clarification; the session-boundary rule for fixing (stage 9 uses a fresh session) is more visible in the separate fixing file.
design_decisions.rationale: Two files match the two sub-modes naturally; one big SKILL.md would conflate the executing and fixing content. The role identity stays short; the sub-modes stay focused. The session-boundary rule (fixing is a fresh session) is more visible in a separate file.

design_decisions.area: Why M122's atomic-writes.md is a separate file from executing.md (cross-cutting contract, not sub-mode):
design_decisions.choice: atomic-writes.md is documented as a cross-cutting contract that applies to BOTH executing and fixing sub-modes (every mp invocation in either goes through the M113 advisory flock lock and the M117 killpg contract). The naming as a separate file is for navigability, not because it's a sub-mode per se — the agent enters executing or fixing and the atomic-write contract is always in effect. The label "third sub-mode file" is misleading and is being retired; atomic-writes.md is a cross-cutting reference doc, parallel to the executing/fixing deep-dives.
design_decisions.rationale: Three sub-mode files (executing, fixing, atomic-writes) match the three concerns naturally. The atomic-writes file is the closest to the 'meta' of the runner role — every mp invocation in either sub-mode goes through the lock and the killpg contract. Splitting it out keeps the procedural sub-modes focused on their lifecycle.

design_decisions.area: Why M98's existing content (claim/execute) moves to M122:
design_decisions.choice: M98's `claim → step done → AC pass → complete` content is the executing sub-mode. M98 is archived per the user's two-agent / four-role architecture. M122's executing.md is the canonical home for that content; M98's historical content stays in git history (the JSON file is preserved at master-plan/archive/milestones/ via `mp milestone archive`).
design_decisions.rationale: M98 was a monolithic skill covering 8 stages. Splitting into per-role skills means the executing-specific stages belong to the runner role, not to the cross-role timeline. M122 is the formalization of that split for the runner side.

findings.description: fix_cycle_wrong_complete: fixing.md Stage 10 hand-off section told runner to call mp milestone complete at the end of the fix cycle, but complete is stage 7 only. The fix cycle ends with milestone verify and the d hand-off to coordinator.

five_canonical_four_listed: executing.md heading said five canonical commands but table listed only 4. Self-review mp reviews finding add is covered in stage 6 separately, not part of the execution table. Renamed to four canonical execution commands.
ambiguous_stage_transition_wording: SKILL.md said lifecycle transitions to self-reviewed (stage 6-7) which was ambiguous. Reworded to be explicit about which stage moves to which.

executing.md has a stale five-vs-four inconsistency that the prior F-02 finding did not fully resolve. Line 3-4 says "The five canonical mp commands walk through each stage." Line 12 says "### The four canonical execution commands" with a table listing only 4 rows (set-status, step done, criterion pass, complete). The 5th canonical command (mp reviews finding add --phase self at stage 6 — the self-review step) is described in the prose at line 58-60 ("mp reviews finding add <id> --phase self ...") but not in the table. F-02 status=fixed but fixed_in is empty — no commit actually closed it. Remediation: either (a) change line 3-4 from "five" to "four" to match the table, or (b) add the 5th row to the table: `mp reviews finding add <id> --phase self --severity ... --category ... --desc "..."` (Self-review at stage 6; files self-detected issues). Option (b) is the substantive fix — the 5 commands are the canonical sequence per AC-02 description ("claim -> step done -> criterion pass -> self-review -> complete").

findings.description: AC-02 verification (`grep -c "mp milestone|mp reviews" templates/skills/mp-runner/executing.md | awk "$1 >= 5"`) counts all occurrences of the substrings "mp milestone" or "mp reviews" in the file. The intent of AC-02 ("FIVE canonical mp commands") is to verify five distinct commands are referenced, not five mentions. A file with the same command mentioned five times (or with five unrelated mentions of "mp milestone" in a different context) would pass. This is a verification design gap — same class as M120 F-01/F-02 and the original M122 F-02. Mitigation: the runner_role_skill.rs test (crates/mp/tests/runner_role_skill.rs:44-77) does assert the 5 distinct commands explicitly (set-status, step done, criterion pass, mp reviews finding add, complete) — that test is the strong defense. The AC-02 verification string is a brittle fallback. Remediation: amend AC-02 verification to point at the test assertion: `cargo test -p mp --test runner_role_skill mp_runner_walks_execute_then_fixing` (analogous to the M120 F-02 fix).
